SPECIAL MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
MONDAY - OCTOBER 5, 2020 -
07:00 P.M.
TELECONFERENCE MEETING AUTHORIZED BY STATE OF CALIFORNIA EXECUTIVE ORDERS N-25-20 AND N-29-20 VIA ZOOM VIDEO COMMUNICATIONS, MEETING ID #868 6308 7784
*COVID-19 NOTICE*
To protect public health and safety during the local, state, and federally declared COVID-19 emergency, the City Council Chamber is closed to the public. Consistent with State of California Executive Orders N-25-20 and N-29-20 and the Los Angeles County Health Officer’s “Safer at Home Order for Control of COVID-19” the City Council will participate in the meeting through teleconference. Public participation in the meeting will be facilitated through the electronic methods as described below.
Agenda Materials:
The agenda and agenda packet related to items on this agenda are available for public inspection at www.cerritos.us. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet will be made available for public inspection at www.cerritos.us.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION:
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us and on Cerritos TV3.
Public Comments:
Members of the public may provide public comment through the following methods:
Email: Members of the public may provide public comment by submitting an email to city_clerk@cerritos.us by 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the meeting date and agenda item number for which you would like to provide comment in the subject line of the email. The public comment will be distributed to all members of the City Council. During the meeting your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Teleconference Participation: You may provide audio public comment by connecting to the teleconference meeting online or by telephone/mobile call (please select only one method). Public speakers will be queued to provide comment at the appropriate time on the agenda. You must be available to provide comment at the time you are called upon to speak. If you are not planning on providing public comment we encourage you to observe the meeting via livestream or on Cerritos TV3 to allow staff to more effectively manage the number of teleconference connections.
Cerritos Zoom meeting online link: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/86863087784
Cerritos Zoom Meeting call-in telephone number: (669) 900-6833
Cerritos Zoom Meeting ID: 868 6308 7784
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations:
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the teleconference meeting.

MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD ON MONDAY,
OCTOBER 5, 2020, 7:00 P.M., TELECONFERENCED MEETING AUTHORIZED BY STATE OF
CALIFORNIA EXECUTIVE ORDERS N-25-20 AND N-29-20, VIA ZOOM VIDEO
COMMUNICATIONS, MEETING ID# 868 6308 7784

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor Naresh Solanki.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Bruce Barrows
  Council/Agency Member Grace Hu
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Chuong Vo
  Mayor/Chair Naresh Solanki

5.  Presentations/Appointments

  Proclamations were made by the City Council as follows:

  Kay Halsey (100th birthday).

  Friends of the Cerritos Library (National Friends of Libraries Week).

  Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer, presented an informational update on the November 3,
  2020 General Election. A PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Written correspondence
  (Written correspondence is considered public record and full-text copies of submitted
  written correspondence can be obtained in the Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer)

  Frank Lee submitted written correspondence requesting City Council endorsement of
  Proposition 20 on the November 3, 2020 Statewide General Election ballot.

  Audio public comments

  Shiva Bhatt, representing the Friends of the Cerritos Library, thanked the City Council
  for honoring their organization with a proclamation in honor of National Friends of
  Libraries Week.
 City of Cerritos  October 5, 2020
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 2 of 8

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions (continued)

  Mary Buell expressed concern with auto test driving activities on Dumont Street.

  Matthew Ellis expressed concern with the deteriorating condition of the Civic Center
  parking lot and parking structure.

  Raymond Kim requested City Council endorsement of Proposition 20 on the
  November 3, 2020 Statewide General Election ballot.

  Jim Bockholt requested City Council endorsement of Proposition 20 on the November
  3, 2020 Statewide General Election ballot.

7.  Consent Calendar

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of September
  24, 2020 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of September 24, 2020
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.  Approval of the Register of Demands

7B.1. Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated September 24, 2020
  (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to approve the Register of
  Demands, as follows:

  City of Cerritos  10/5/2020  $ 5,435,817.80 (COUNCIL)

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

(minutes continue on next page)
 City of Cerritos  October 5, 2020
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 3 of 8

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7C.  Approval of Treasurer’s Reports

  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Treasurer’s Reports for the period ending
  August 31, 2020 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Treasurer’s Reports for the period ending August 31, 2020
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7D.  Award of contract for water quality analyses and laboratory services, RFP No. 1409-20
  (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to:

  1. Award a professional services contract in the amount of $38,478.00 for Water Quality
  Analyses and Laboratory Services, RFP No. 1409-20, to Enthalpy Analytical for a period
  of two (2) years with the option to renew for three (3) one (1) year terms and reject the
  other proposal; and

  2. Authorize the Mayor to execute the agreement on behalf of the City of Cerritos; and

  3. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute any contract modifications that
  may be necessary to complete the specified scope of work (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

8A.  Review and consideration of an appeal by project applicant Kia of Cerritos of the
  Planning Commission decision (Planning Commission Resolution No. P.C. 2020-9)
  denying a proposal for an automobile repair use located at 10742, 10750 and 10754
  Artesia Boulevard, currently zoned Industrial (M) (APN 7034-018-117 and APN 7034-
  018-009), and all related entitlements, including General Plan Amendment 2020-1,
  Development Plan Amendment 2020-1, and Conditional Use Permit 2020-1
  (COUNCIL).*

  *This public hearing is continued from the City Council Regular Meeting of
  September 24, 2020

  Staff reports were given by Robert Lopez, Director of Community Development, Kristin
  Aguila, Advance Planning/Economic Development Manager, and Sandy Cisneros, Senior
  Planner. A PowerPoint presentation was displayed.
 City of Cerritos  October 5, 2020
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 4 of 8

8.  Public Hearings (continued)

8A.  (continued)

  The Mayor opened the continued public hearing and public comments period.

  New written correspondence submitted subsequent to the original September 24, 2020
  public hearing date
  (Written correspondence is considered public record and full-text copies of submitted
  written correspondence can be obtained in the Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer)

  Eddie Nagahashi submitted written correspondence in opposition to approval of the
  appeal submitted by Kia of Cerritos of the Planning Commission’s decision on this
  matter.

  Troy Stahl submitted written correspondence requesting that condition of approval no.
  55 should include language prohibiting employee parking on Dumont Avenue.

  Audio public comments

  Jon Matson, representing the appellant Kia of Cerritos, stated City staff has worked
  diligently at resolving the concerns of the respective parties related to the project and
  noted he was available to answer any questions.

  Mary Buell, representing B & B Stables, stated she appreciated the work completed on
  this project by staff and the other parties. She requested clarification regarding activity
  at the proposed facility which may be occur on holidays and whether the facility would
  be closed. She noted her agreement with the proposed conditions of approval and
  requested whether the zoning could revert back to “M” zoning if the property were sold
  in the future.

  Kirk Benson, representing Kia of Cerritos, thanked the staff for their hard work on this
  project and noted the auto repair use would not be open during the holidays. The
  storage portion of the facility would be occasionally accessed during the holidays to
  retrieve any vehicles for sale.

  Troy Stahl, representing Valley Christian School, thanked staff for their hard work on
  this project. He stated that also they did provide comment on various stipulations
  related to the project, the primary concern of the school is the safety of their students
  and the position of the school is that this project is not in the best interest in the school.
  They will support the ultimate position of the City and urged the enforcement of the
  conditions of approval in the future.

  Teresa Herrera, representing B & B Stables, requested clarification regarding the
  operating hours of Kia of Cerritos on Saturdays and Sundays, as B & B Stables was
  assured there would be no activity on Saturday and Sundays, although the speaker from
  Kia of Cerritos mentioned earlier this evening that there would be some vehicle retrieval
  activity on the weekends.

  Kirk Benson, representing Kia of Cerritos, responded to the previous speaker by stating
  that the auto repair activity is limited to Monday through Friday, from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00
  p.m. There may be occasional retrieval of a specific car for sale on a weekend or holiday.
  He also confirmed new vehicle delivery only occurs at the Kia of Cerritos “Edison”
  facility.

  Mel Cortez expressed concern for the students of Valley Christian School as related to
  the number of cars and traffic impacts of the auto dealerships, including driving tests,
  on Dumont Avenue.
 City of Cerritos  October 5, 2020
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 5 of 8

8.  Public Hearings (continued)

8A.  (continued)

  Kirk Benson, representing Kia of Cerritos, stated in his closing comments that Kia of
  Cerritos will be a great neighbor, they have implemented a “zero-tolerance” policy for all
  employees regarding test driving on Dumont Avenue, and will abide by all approved
  conditions of approval.

  Noting there were no other individuals who provided written correspondence or elected
  to speak, the Mayor declared the public hearing and public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Hu, and seconded by Barrows, to:

  1. Approve Kia of Cerritos’ appeal and reverse the decision of the Planning Commission;
  and

  2. Waive full reading of and adopt Resolution No. 2020-26, A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AMENDING THE CERRITOS GENERAL PLAN LAND
  USE MAP BY CHANGING THE LAND USE DESIGNATION OF TWO (2)
  ADJACENT PARCELS, MEASURING APPROXIMATELY ±1.35 ACRES IN TOTAL,
  LOCATED AT 10742, 10750, AND 10754 ARTESIA BOULEVARD (APNS 7034-
  018-009,  7034-018-117),  FROM  LIGHT  INDUSTRIAL  TO
  INDUSTRIAL/COMMERCIAL, HEREIN REFERENCED AS GENERAL PLAN
  AMENDMENT 2020-1 (COUNCIL); and

  3. Waive full reading of and introduce Ordinance No. 1034, AN ORDINANCE OF THE
  CITY OF CERRITOS AMENDING THE CERRITOS DEVELOPMENT MAP BY
  CHANGING THE ZONE CLASSIFICATION OF TWO (2) ADJACENT PARCELS,
  MEASURING APPROXIMATELY ±1.35 ACRES IN TOTAL, LOCATED AT 10742,
  10750, AND 10754 ARTESIA BOULEVARD (APNS 7034-018-009, 7034-018-
  117), FROM INDUSTRIAL (M) TO INDUSTRIAL/COMMERCIAL (MC), HEREIN
  REFERENCED AS DEVELOPMENT MAP AMENDMENT 2020-1 (COUNCIL); and

  4. Waive full reading of and adopt Resolution No. 2020-27, A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL APPROVING CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT 2020-1, A
  REQUEST BY APPLICANT KIA OF CERRITOS, ON BEHALF OF THE PROPERTY
  OWNER, TO PERMIT AUTOMOTIVE REPAIR, WAREHOUSING, AND OFFICE
  USES AT 10742, 10750, AND 10754 ARTESIA BOULEVARD, CERRITOS,
  CALIFORNIA, 90703. THE SUBJECT PROPERTY IS PROPOSED TO BE RE-
  ZONED FROM INDUSTRIAL (M) TO INDUSTRIAL/COMMERCIAL (MC) UNDER
  DEVELOPMENT MAP AMENDMENT 2020-1 (APN 7034-018-117 AND APN
  7034-018-009) (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  (minutes continue on next page)
 City of Cerritos  October 5, 2020
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 6 of 8

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of an informational update on the City's response to the
  COVID-19 local emergency (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Annie Hylton, City & Theater Marketing Manager/City
  Librarian. A PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  provided written correspondence or elected to speak, the Mayor declared the public
  comments period closed.

  There was no further action taken on this item.

9B.  Review and consideration of an access and license agreement between the City of
  Cerritos and the Water Replenishment District for the installation of a groundwater
  monitoring well at Cerritos Park East (COUNCIL).

  Staff reports were given by Kanna Vancheswaran, Director of Public Works/Water &
  Power, and Ana Tenorio, Management Analyst. A PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Brian Partington, Water Replenishment District, noted the agency will follow the
  California Well Standard for addressing abandoned wells.

  Noting there were no individuals who provided written correspondence or elected to
  speak, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Hu, to:

  1.  Take no action on the proposed access and license agreement at this time; and

  2.  Direct staff to develop language to be included in the proposed access and license
  agreement which stipulates requirements for well abandonment; and

  3.  Place the access and license agreement between the City of Cerritos and the Water
  Replenishment District for the installation of a groundwater monitoring well at
  Cerritos Park East, as amended to include the stipulated requirements for well
  abandonment, on a future agenda for City Council review and consideration
  (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 – 1) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  Yokoyama
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9C.  Review and consideration of an award of contract for the fabrication and installation of
  new bulkheads for the Cerritos Olympic Swim Center, Project No. 20201, Bid No. 1408-
  20 (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kanna Vancheswaran, Director of Public Works/Water &
  Power. A PowerPoint presentation was displayed.
 City of Cerritos  October 5, 2020
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 7 of 8

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9C.  (continued)

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  provided written correspondence or elected to speak, the Mayor declared the public
  comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Hu, and seconded by Yokoyama, to:

  1.  Reject all bids for Project No. 20201, Bid No. 1408-20, fabrication and installation
  of new bulkheads for the Cerritos Olympic Swim Center; and

  2.  Direct staff to re-evaluate and modify the scope of the project, and to re-advertise
  for bid at a future date (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 – 1) as follows:

  AYES:  Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  Barrows
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

10.  Legislative Items

10A.  Report on pending legislation.

  None.

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or

  None.

11.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings

  Reports were provided by Councilmember Barrows, Hu, and Yokoyama, Mayor Pro Tem

  CONSENSUS (Barrows): Directed the City Manager to add City Council consideration

  City Attorney Mark Steres announced the City Council would recess to Closed Session to

  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54957 (COUNCIL)
